summary: Dominic Sur is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen C. Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chonam. He held a post at Utah State University.

Indologist Dominik Wujastyk studied at the University of London and University of Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1985–2007), University of London (~1984–2007), University College London (2002–2009), University of Vienna (2009–2015), and University of Alberta (2015).
Dominique Sportiche is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1979–1984). He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles from around 1988.

Dominique-Sila Khan was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She served as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies from circa 1993 to 2016.
Don A. Pittman works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was a doctoral candidate at the University of Chicago and served on the faculty at Texas Christian University.

Don Handelman is an anthropologist and scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and was Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe was an Indologist, archaeologist, and linguist. Educated at Richmond College and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, he served as epigraphist for the Government of Sri Lanka (~1899–1928) and taught at the University of London (~1917–1936).

Donald A. Ringe is a linguist who studied at the University of Kentucky, University of Oxford, and Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He taught Classics at Bard College (1983–1985) and joined the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1985.

Donald Anthony Low was an historian and Indologist who studied at Exeter College and Clare Hall, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex (~1964–1973), Australian National University (~1973–1982), and the University of Cambridge (~1983–1994).

Donald Capps was a religious studies scholar who studied at Lewis & Clark, Yale, and Chicago. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago, UNC Charlotte, and Phillips University, before serving at Princeton Theological Seminary from 1981 to 2009.

Donald Edward Gjertson is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University (attested 1975) and held a post at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (attested 1989).

Donald Harper is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He held an appointment at the University of Arizona (attested 1999) and serves as Centennial Professor of Chinese Studies at the University of Chicago (attested 2026).

Donald K. Swearer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at Swarthmore College (~1970–2004) and served as a Distinguished Visiting Fellow at Harvard Divinity School's Center for the Study of World Religions (2004–2010).

Donald Keene was a Japanologist who studied at Columbia University and Harvard University, learning under William Theodore de Bary. He held appointments at the University of Cambridge (1949–1954) and Columbia University from 1955.

Donald Phillip Verene is a philosopher who studied at Knox College and Washington University in St. Louis. He served as department chair at Emory University (1982–1988) and held visiting posts at Pembroke College, Oxford (1988) and Sapienza University of Rome (1996).

Donald R. Davis Jr. is an Indologist who studied under Richard W. Lariviere, Patrick Olivelle, and Ludo Rocher. He held faculty posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2012) and the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned his degrees at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He taught at Middlebury College (1986) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Michigan in 1990.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima was an individual who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Dongak Tendzin was a figure who both studied under and taught Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
